Digital accessibility, explained

Web accessibility

Digital accessibility means designing sites and applications usable by as many people as possible, including people with disabilities (visual, auditory, motor, cognitive). An accessible web actually benefits every user: older people, people with a limited connection, people using a mobile device or an assistive technology, and anyone browsing under less than ideal conditions.

The WCAG

The WCAG are organized into 4 principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust (POUR). Each success criterion is rated A, AA, or AAA. This document targets level AA conformance, the most widely referenced standard (used in most legislation, notably in Europe, the United States, and Canada).

Using this document

Fixing findings

Findings are ranked by severity. Start with critical findings, which fully block some people from using the page, before addressing major issues, then moderate, then minor. When possible, findings include a concrete fix your team (in-house or a technical provider) can apply. Once fixes are in place, retest the page (notably with keyboard tabbing and a screen reader) to confirm the issue is actually resolved.

PDF export

A direct PDF export is in the works. In the meantime, your browser's print function (Ctrl/Cmd+P) produces a faithful PDF version, with columns and colors preserved.

Why an HTML document?

This report is a self-contained HTML file rather than a standard PDF: it opens in any browser, works offline once downloaded, adapts to light or dark mode, and stays readable with a screen reader. The links on this page (shortcuts, appendices) let you jump straight to the section you need.

Appendices

The appendices hold the raw data from the automated scans run during the audit, in a technical format that isn't meant to be read as-is. They serve as evidence and reference: your technical team can check a specific result there, but you don't need to understand them to understand the report.

Questions about this document? Write to contact@vesperlab.dev

Findings and recommendations

1 finding(s) retained in this report.

  • ◆ Critical : 0
  • ▲ Major : 1
  • ● Moderate : 0
  • ▪ Minor : 0

Interactive elements (links, buttons, form fields) show no visual keyboard focus indicator, or one that is insufficiently visible. Here, there is no visible focus around the clickable images.

▲ Major

WCAG criterion: 2.4.7 — Focus Visible

Impact: People navigating by keyboard lose track of their position on the page, making the site difficult or even impossible to use without a mouse. Here, navigation is still possible by pressing Enter (the image opens without the user having seen it was focused) or by pressing Tab once more (to reach the next button), which adds clicks and can lose the user.

Fix: Never remove the browser's focus outline without replacing it. Provide a clear indicator on every interactive element, visible against every background on the page. A well-contrasted `:focus-visible` style often does the job.

Occurrences noted: 3

Summary

As of now, the site achieves AA conformance on 34 of the 35 applicable criteria. The only non-conformant criterion concerns focus visibility, with a fix planned by November 2, 2026. These results follow from a diagnosis and an accessibility statement, whose results follow below.

--

I audited the HTML prototype of the site (vesperlab.dev) as part of producing its accessibility statement, between September 29, 2026 and October 1 of the same year. This diagnosis covers the complete site and its repeated elements, in the prototype's current state, and technical recommendations will be provided for the fix.

It covers the following pages:
- Home, About, The Lab and Contact;
- Blog, plus one blog post with its illustration;
- one page from each of the Tools and Projects sections, which share the same template;
using the tools listed in the resources, and the in-house tool Vesper Auditor. Tests were run with VoiceOver (macOS) on Safari, Chrome and Zen. The NVDA, JAWS and TalkBack screen readers were not tested.

Following this audit, an accessibility diagnosis and its statement were produced on October 1, as an HTML page. That page was then itself analyzed as an additional page of the site, from October 2 to 5, 2026. Its results were added to the final document, and the original diagnosis can be viewed in the follow-up section.

This site is a special case: it is our own. I audited it myself, which has its limits, but which also allowed me to improve my tools along the way, including the ones offered publicly. The original prototype was not modified between this report and its publication online. Changes may have been made to the site since publication that are not yet reflected in this statement.

--
On the positive side, the site includes many additions that build accessibility into its content.

Navigation. In the header, it lets you skip to the content (skip link) and quickly reach the accessibility options. In the footer, a site map shows the sub-menus, right next to the accessibility options: text size, the moon movement in the background, light or dark theme. On the light theme, however, the moon's shadow is more visible and the rendering less polished.

Languages. A language option switches the site to English. The company is based in Quebec (Canada), where both French-speaking and English-speaking people live: visitors' assistive technologies can therefore be set to either language. When visiting the English version, a message clearly announces that the content is not translated and offers a button to a translation tool. If the person keeps reading, the announced language is the right one.

Structure. The instructions announced to the screen reader are clear. The landmarks, headings and labels are consistent and well defined.

Images. Particular attention was paid to images, with two distinct choices:
- The mockups have an empty alternative text, in favor of the surrounding context. Each one is a link, clearly named by `aria-label`, that lets you enlarge it.
- In the blog, the image has an alternative text that differs from its caption, which explains its content.

--

A fix is needed for criterion 2.4.7 (Focus Visible) to reach conformance.

On the pages that display mockups (Lab > Tools; Lab > Projects) and on the About page, the focus does not appear around the images, which are links that enlarge them in a new window. While tabbing, the focus can be seen moving forward to the image, disappearing, then reappearing on the next element. When the focus is invisible on the image, the link still works with the Enter key and is correctly announced thanks to its `aria-label`.

The people affected are those who can see the screen and navigate by keyboard with the Tab key: for example, people with reduced mobility or low vision. They lose their place on the page.

To fix it, the same `:focus-visible` approach just needs to be applied to the clickable images in the Tools and Projects sections and in the About block. The proposed deadline is one month from this statement, i.e. November 2, 2026.

--

In the prototype's current state and after the diagnosis, the site is partially AA conformant. Several points were nevertheless noted during the diagnosis, with no direct impact on the site's accessibility. These are flags from automated scans that turned out to be false positives:
- The image and label scans report an image with no alt, named "X" in the web structure scans. It is the icon of the close button of the image enlargement window. This button is accessible and works in its context. It is hidden otherwise, except during automated scans.
- The mockups are links, so that they can be enlarged. Without clicking the link, the image's description relies on the context. The link itself is clear and correctly announced.

--
The difficulty of this diagnosis lies in objectively judging one's own product. Conversely, it is easy to assure my readers that these fixes will be made, and that this assessment, besides giving me a fresh look at my own work, helps me improve my method and my tools for the future.

End of the original diagnosis, which led to the accessibility statement. That statement was then itself audited; the results follow:
--

I audited the accessibility statement of the vesperlab.dev site, from October 2 to 5, 2026. This diagnosis covers the statement alone, in HTML format, attached to the site and based on it. No accessibility barrier was found. A few optional improvement points are noted below.

The audit covers a single page, using the tools listed in the resources and the in-house tool Vesper Auditor. It was carried out under the same conditions as the site's: VoiceOver (macOS) on Safari, Chrome and Zen, without NVDA, JAWS or TalkBack.

--

On the positive side, the accessibility statement, despite a format that differs from the site's, is consistent with it. To make navigation easier and avoid long scrolling, it offers shortcuts at the top of the page, and consistently reuses the option to change the page theme.

One point of attention. The conformance tables show a very slight horizontal scroll (73 px according to 🦇 Reflow, sometimes less, or even none depending on the browser and tool used). Criterion 1.4.10 (Reflow) does not apply to data tables, which are correctly accessible and readable here. So, in my view, there is no immediate improvement possible to change this horizontal scroll without harming the readability already established for the tables. A rearrangement of the content could nevertheless be discussed internally to improve how statements read on mobile.

--

In conclusion:

  • As of October 1, 2026, vesperlab.dev, without its accessibility statement, is partially conformant at AA level: 34 of the 35 applicable criteria are met.
  • As of October 5, 2026, vesperlab.dev with its accessibility statement has the same result: 34 of 35 criteria met.

A major fix is due by November 2, 2026 to make the site conformant with criterion 2.4.7 Focus Visible. It maps to the following standards: RGAA 4.1: 7.3 and 10.7; EN 301 549: 9.2.4.7; SGQRI 008 3.0: 2.4.7.

The accessibility statement will be updated once this fix has been verified.

Accessibility statement

Conformance status

This site is partially conformant with WCAG 2.2 level AA: non-conformant items are listed below.

34/35 applicable criteria conformant (level AA).

Scope of the evaluation

Pages tested
  • Home — Home — vesperlab.dev/
  • About — Toggle-Page — /a-propos/
  • The Lab — Hub — /le-lab/
  • Vesper Tools — Card-List — /le-lab/outils/
  • Projects — Card-List — /le-lab/realisations/
  • Blog — Blog-Index — /blog/
  • Blog post — Blog-Post — /blog/essayer-evoluer-recommencer/
  • Contact — Toggle-Page — /contact/
  • Shared elements — Shared — /
  • Accessibility Statement — A11Y — /declaration-accessibilite/
Evaluator
Pauline Cvt (VesperLab)
Period
2026-09-29 – 2026-10-05
Method
Manual evaluation against WCAG 2.2, carried out using one or more browsers, screen readers, and audit assistance tools.

Non-accessible content

  • 2.4.7 — Focus Visible : About : Lost at the img · Vesper Tools : no focus border around img · Projects : no focus border around img

Remediation plan

Fix planned by November 2, 2026: adding a visible focus outline on the clickable images of the Vesper Tools, Projects and About pages.

This statement will be updated once the fix has been verified.

Feedback and contact information

To report an accessibility issue or make a request about this site's content, contact:

Pauline Cvt, gérante — contact@vesperlab.dev

This report includes the accessibility statement rating. To this end, an initial audit was conducted on the website to generate a first draft of this report. That draft was then audited itself and added to the original report.

Report produced with Vesper Auditor, VesperLab.
